title: State commission authorizes agreement with Ecru police on license plate readers
excerpt: All three transportation commissioners voted yes Nov. 10. The vote authorizes the executive director to sign an agreement covering state highway right-of-way.
locality: Ecru Police Department in Pontotoc County, Mississippi. The commission acted at its state meeting.

paragraphs.text: Mississippi’s three transportation commissioners voted Nov. 10 to authorize an agreement with the Ecru Police Department for automatic license plate readers or other permanently mounted law enforcement equipment on state highway right-of-way. MDOT’s public index lists Nov. 19 as the update date for the meeting minutes.

Willie Simmons, John Caldwell and Charles Busby each voted yes. The motion authorizes the executive director to sign a memorandum of understanding with the Ecru department. It also names the Pelahatchie Police Department in Rankin County for an agreement of its own.

The vote gives state officials authority to make the agreement. The minutes do not say whether Ecru has installed any readers, when equipment might go into service or what the local project would cost.

Readers can request MDOT’s records on the agreement through the department’s public records form. The department asks for details such as the location and time period. The Nov. 10 meeting date and the Ecru Police Department identify the item in the commission minutes.
